title: Scheduler handshake race causing compactor index flip and fp16 accumulation skew under speculative batching
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Summary:
We observe intermittent correctness failures (token mis-ordering, duplicated tokens, and small but measurable numerical drift in logits) under high-concurrency workloads after recent speculative-batching and compactor optimizations. Failures are low-frequency but reproduce reliably in our stress harness when speculative batching is enabled and the compactor runs concurrently with prefill->decode handshakes. Impact: customer-facing flakiness for streaming endpoints and occasional semantic regressions in decoder outputs.

Repro steps (stress harness):
1) Checkout runtime branch with speculative-batching enabled (use test tag runtime-spec-2026).
2) Start stress harness: ./tools/stress_runner --model=gpt-medium --sequence=1024 --clients=120 --concurrency=40 --speculative=1 --cycles=10000
3) Inject compaction interval short: REDWOOD_COMPACTOR_INTERVAL_MS=12 and REDWOOD_FORCE_COMPACT=1
4) Observe harness assertion failures or check logs for "compactor:index-flip" or mismatched kv-slot ownership.

Observed symptoms / telemetry:
- Token reordering correlated with compaction short windows and elevated scheduler preemption.
- Log lines showing index transitions without corresponding ownership handoffs: "compactor: swapping index without fence" (repro sample attached).
- Small but consistent logit drift (fp16 path) versus fp32 baseline on same request trace (~0.3-0.8% L2 change) after index flip events.
- Error bursts coincide with kernel-selection retries and 5xx returns in hosted telemetry.

Initial investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally with the harness. Failures cluster when speculative-batching is enabled and kernel-selection path uses the lightweight compactor to reclaim slab slots.
- Hypothesis: compactor performs an index rotation that is not properly synchronized with in-flight decoder kernels. When a decoder read/writes the slab concurrently with the rotation, an in-flight kernel may operate on a stale or reclaimed slot. That leads to token duplication/reordering and non-deterministic FP accumulation because different kernels touch memory with mixed precision ordering.
- Evidence: heap snapshots show slab slots reused while reference counters for the slot are still >0. Traces show a compactor.Index = 13 -> 0 swap while a decoder thread still reports ownership of slot 13.
- The kernel-selection fast path assumes a read-mostly index and uses relaxed atomics; compactor does a blind write. On some hardware (older AMD/ARM test infra) this manifests more frequently.

Temporary mitigations implemented (short-term hotfix):
- Patch applied to disable speculative-batching for release-2026.02 builds (flag REDWOOD_SPECULATIVE=0) until root cause fixed.
- Added a compactor mutex and CPU memory fence around index rotation in the hotfix branch (runtime/hotfix/compactor-fence). This eliminates reproductions in CI stress for short runs but caused a modest latency P1 regression under 99th percentile (+6ms).
- Added alerting (metrics) for compactor-index-rotation-count and slab-ownership-mismatch metric.

Root cause theory (current working hypothesis):
1) Compactor swaps a single index word to indicate the new active slab without using a full-release memory fence and without bumping per-slot version tags.
2) Decoder kernels on the fast path read the index and then start using the slab; a concurrent compaction can reclaim the physical page and reassign it to a new logical slot. The decoder continues to write/read the now-reused memory.
3) Mixed-precision FP16 kernels interleave writes that are ordered differently than FP32 accumulation, causing tiny numeric drift which accumulates across decoding steps and becomes observable as output drift.
4) Under heavy prefill->decode scheduling pressure, handshakes are reordered (scheduler yields mid-handshake) so the window of vulnerability increases.

Proposed long-term fixes (plan):
- Design: Move to versioned-slot model: every slab slot carries a 64-bit epoch counter incremented on assignment. Decode path validates epoch tag before assuming ownership and re-reads if mismatch. This is the preferred correctness-first approach.
- Implementation: Add atomic 64-bit slot tag and require the decoder kernel to perform a validate-and-claim sequence (compare-exchange or double-read fence). This avoids global mutexes and preserves throughput.
- Kernel change: Make fast-path kernel selection use ephemeral reservation which increments slot epoch before kernel launches (lightweight atomic). Decoders abort and retry on epoch mismatch (rare).
- Scheduler change: Tighten handshake ordering by adding a short scheduling yield on prefill completion to allow compactor to observe stable slots (micro-optimization to reduce vulnerability window).
- QA: Expand stress harness to cover mixed-precision paths (fp16 and fp32), various architectures (x86, AMD, ARM), and run for 48h in CI.

Acceptance criteria:
- No reproductions in stress harness running 48h across all test infra with speculative-batching enabled and compactor_interval=12ms.
- No slab-ownership-mismatch alerts in staging for 2 weeks.
- <2% perf regression on 99th percentile latency compared to baseline; if >2% provide mitigation plan.

Work items / timeline:
- [Day 0-2] Root cause confirmation and more deterministic repro harness (Liam) - DONE (logs attached).
- [Day 3-6] Implement versioned-slot prototype and unit tests (Liam + Priya) - IN PROGRESS.
- [Day 7-10] Kernel integration and micro-benchmarking; validate atomic cost and retry rate (Nikhil) - TODO.
- [Day 11-14] Roll out to canary staging, run 48h stress, monitor metrics (SRE) - TODO.
- [Day 15] Merge and release with rollback plan (PM sign-off) - TODO.

Rollout / mitigation strategy:
- Merge versioned-slot after micro-bench signoff. Canary on dedicated pools with speculative enabled and compactor interval lowered. Monitor slab-ownership-mismatch and token-ordering alerts. If retry rates >1% revert and investigate further.

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Global mutex on compactor is simplest but increases tail latency. We prefer versioned-slot to keep throughput.
- Adding epoch validation adds a retry path; worst-case extra decode retry cost must be quantified. Expectation is <0.1% retry rate in normal traffic.

Acceptance criteria for closing ticket (QA checklist):
- [ ] Versioned-slot landed and unit-tested.
- [ ] Kernel-level validate-and-claim integrated with decoder.
- [ ] 48h stress pass across infra tiers with no reproductions.
- [ ] Monitoring shows no slab-ownership-mismatch for 2 weeks in staging.
- [ ] PM and SRE sign-off for canary and production rollout.
